body.text: Multi-stop Türkiye routes quickly reveal the hassle of hauling 23 kg suitcases across cobblestones and 15 kg domestic flight allowances. Storing heavy bags or shipping fragile purchases directly home keeps intercity transfers light.
Where can you store large suitcases safely at IST, SAW and central Istanbul?

Istanbul Airport (IST) runs 24/7 left-luggage offices on the Arrivals floor (opposite Exit 13 and near the domestic exit) plus Departures lockers near Gates 1 and 6. Sabiha Gökçen (SAW) operates a 24/7 baggage deposit on Departures, while central Istanbul uses hotel bell desks and vetted storage apps.

According to [iGA Istanbul Airport's 2026 left-luggage tariff](https://www.istairport.com/en/services/discover/airport-facilities/left-luggage-offices-and-storage-lockers?locale=en), official rates scale clearly by bag size:

body.text: Airport offices X-ray every bag and issue a numbered claim tag—keep a photo of that tag on your phone in case the paper slip goes missing.
Can you ship carpets or ceramics internationally from Türkiye safely?

Yes—established carpet galleries in Istanbul and Cappadocia and ceramic workshops in Avanos or İznik routinely ship door-to-door worldwide via DHL Express, FedEx, or UPS with full transit insurance, arriving in Europe or North America in 4 to 7 business days. Always insist on a traceable air waybill, written insurance value, and a formal commercial invoice before paying.
Two legal and practical rules protect your purchase:

items: Antiquities ban (Law No. 2863): Exporting cultural artefacts or antique rugs older than 100 years without a Ministry of Culture and Tourism museum directorate certificate is illegal in Türkiye and carries severe criminal penalties ([Letfix Customs Guide](https://letfix.app/guide/items-prohibited-from-bringing-into-turkey); [Bıçak Law Firm](https://www.bicakhukuk.com/en/illicit-traffic-of-cultural-property-in-turkish-law/)). Never buy a "vintage" carpet or coin if the seller brushes off documentation.

VAT exemption on direct export: When a licensed dealer exports your carpet directly by courier, they can issue a VAT-free export invoice rather than forcing you to haul it to the airport for a [VAT refund at IST](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/tax-free-shopping-turkey).
Double-boxed ceramics: Insist on foam-in-place or double-walled crating for hand-painted İznik bowls and platters; standard bubble wrap rarely survives airline baggage belts.

body.text: How do hotel bell-desk holds work during Cappadocia side trips?

If your itinerary starts and ends in Istanbul, nearly every four- and five-star Istanbul hotel—and most reputable boutique properties in Karaköy, Beyoğlu, or Sultanahmet—will store your main suitcases free of charge in a locked luggage room while you fly to Cappadocia or Izmir for two to five nights with a light cabin bag.
Confirm by email that you have a return booking; non-returning guests usually get same-day holds only. Pack a collapsible weekender inside your main suitcase for short domestic hops.
What size limits apply on domestic flights and private vans?

Domestic flights enforce tighter weights than international tickets: standard economy on Turkish Airlines and Pegasus Airlines typically includes 15 kg checked baggage (20 kg on higher tiers) plus an 8 kg cabin bag up to 55 × 40 × 23 cm or 55 × 40 × 20 cm ([Turkish Airlines](https://www.turkishairlines.com/en-int/any-questions/carry-on-baggage/); [Pegasus](https://www.flypgs.com/en/pegasus-baggage-allowance)).

items: Buy extra kilos online early: Pre-paying an extra 5–10 kg in the airline app at least 2 to 8 hours before departure costs a fraction of airport excess-baggage fees, and single bags cannot exceed 32 kg ([Skyscanner Pegasus Guide](https://www.skyscanner.net/flights/advice/pegasus-airlines-baggage-allowance-sizes-fees-and-what-you-can-bring)).

Private Mercedes Vito vs. Sprinter vans: A standard VIP Mercedes Vito seats up to 6 passengers comfortably, but its rear boot fits only 4 to 5 large hard-shell suitcases. For groups of 4+ travellers with full-size luggage, request a long-chassis Mercedes Sprinter from the start so suitcases do not end up stacked on spare seats.

faq.q: Can I leave luggage at Istanbul Airport (IST) for a whole week?
faq.a: Yes. IST's left-luggage offices accept multi-day and multi-week storage, billed in 24-hour increments based on bag size. Expect to pay 550 TRY per day for a standard large checked suitcase.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to store bags at my Istanbul hotel or at IST?
faq.a: Your Istanbul hotel is almost always free if you have a confirmed return booking, and it saves you from paying 550 TRY per bag per day at IST. Only use airport storage if you are not returning to the same hotel.

faq.q: Are luggage storage apps like Bounce or Radical Storage safe in Istanbul?
faq.a: Reputable platforms partner with vetted hotels and shops in central districts like Sultanahmet, Karaköy, and Taksim and include per-bag protection, making them reliable for daytime holds. Always keep passports, cash, and laptops on your person.

faq.q: Can I ship personal suitcases domestically from Istanbul to Bodrum or Cappadocia?
faq.a: Domestic couriers such as Yurtiçi Kargo or Aras Kargo can ship boxes between Turkish hotels, though delivery takes 2–3 business days and requires Turkish-language coordination. Paying for extra airline baggage on a direct flight is usually faster and safer.

faq.q: Do I pay import duty when shipping a Turkish carpet home?
faq.a: Duty depends on your home country's customs thresholds and whether the carpet is handwoven or machine-made. Ask your dealer for an accurate HS tariff code and invoice so your local customs broker clears it cleanly.

faq.q: How much luggage fits in an Istanbul yellow taxi?
faq.a: Standard yellow sedan taxis fit two medium suitcases—or one large suitcase plus two carry-ons—in the boot, especially because many run on LPG tanks that eat into trunk space. Book a private van if you have three or more large bags.
